name: Missed Medication
teaching_point: An out-of-range vital has a simple, traceable cause hiding in the anamnesis (a medication lapse) that the raw alert never reveals. Tests whether the system connects a refill gap in the EHR with a patient-reported lapse.
disclaimer: FICTIONAL DATA ONLY. Educational prototype. Not a diagnosis.

ehr_context.note: Full available EHR for P001 at alert time (mirrors data/patients.json). The EHR agent must select only the relevant subset.

visit_notes.summary: BP controlled at 128/78 in clinic. Reviewed medication list; patient reports good adherence. Continue current regimen. Recheck in 3 months.

anamnesis_context.note: Full available anamnesis for P001 at alert time.

history.narrative: Long-standing high blood pressure and diabetes, usually well controlled at home.

medication_adherence.detail: Reports she ran out of her blood pressure pill about a week ago and has not picked up the refill yet; still taking the diabetes and cholesterol pills.
medication_adherence.barriers: could not get a ride to the pharmacy

patient_concerns.concern: "I feel okay but the machine keeps showing high numbers and it's making me nervous."

gold_brief.alert_summary: Home BP 182/104 mmHg, well above the 160/100 alert limit and far above the patient's 126/76 baseline.

contextual_findings.finding: BP has trended upward over the past week (150/92 -> 164/96 -> 176/100 -> 182/104), not a single isolated spike.
Patient reports she ran out of her blood pressure pill about a week ago and has not refilled it.
Lisinopril 20 mg daily is an active antihypertensive; last refill 2026-05-02 was a 30-day supply, which is consistent with the medication running out around mid-June.
Patient reports a mild headache over the past few days.

possible_contributing_factors.factor: Possible contribution from an antihypertensive medication lapse
possible_contributing_factors.supporting_evidence: Patient-reported that she ran out of her BP pill ~1 week ago; EHR shows lisinopril last refilled 2026-05-02 as a 30-day supply; BP has risen steadily over the same period.
possible_contributing_factors.uncertainty: Self-reported lapse not yet confirmed against pharmacy fill data; other contributors (diet, stress, white-coat effect) not excluded.

data_conflicts.description: The most recent clinic note (2026-04-15) records 'good adherence', whereas the patient now reports a lapse beginning ~1 week ago. These are not necessarily contradictory (different time points) but the change in adherence since the last visit should be noted.

missing_data_and_uncertainty: No serum potassium on file (last labs 2026-04-15 included creatinine/eGFR but not potassium) — relevant when adjusting an ACE inhibitor.
Pharmacy fill/pickup history not available to confirm the reported lapse.
No same-day repeat BP measurement or symptom check for end-organ concern.
suggested_clinician_considerations: Confirm the medication lapse with the patient and/or pharmacy and clarify the barrier to refill (reported lack of transportation).
Consider a repeat BP measurement and ask about red-flag symptoms (severe headache, chest pain, visual changes, focal weakness).
Consider whether recent renal function/electrolytes are needed before resuming/adjusting the ACE inhibitor.

urgency_assessment.rationale: Markedly elevated BP with an upward trend and a plausible, addressable cause; warrants prompt clinician review, though no reported red-flag symptoms.

gold_brief.safety_disclaimer: This Clinical Context Brief is decision support only, generated from fictional data for an educational prototype. It does not provide a diagnosis or treatment recommendation. All clinical judgment remains with the reviewing clinician. Patient-reported items are self-reported and unverified.

gold_checklist: Identifies medication-lapse as a factor to consider (not a diagnosis)
Connects EHR refill date/supply with the patient-reported lapse
Notes the rising BP trend rather than a single reading
Flags missing potassium / pharmacy confirmation as missing data
Contains a safety disclaimer and full traceability
